owner_request: Proposed towns should not dwarf the nearby marked (lore) settlement; the model should take this into account inherently, not by post-hoc swaps.
evidence_seen_before_declaration: Roman AD 150 cohort (664 towns, Greek walls at inhabited share), descriptive only: of 95 towns within 75 km of a provincial capital, 6.3% are larger than it (median size ratio 0.11); 30% of towns are the largest within 75 km; non-dominant towns have median size 0.27 x their local maximum (quartiles 0.12-0.49).

model_H.idea: Sizes are generated as a settlement hierarchy. Centres are drawn first (on the map: the marked campaign places, in lore order, with the capital term; on Earth: the provincial capitals). Every other town draws its size relative to its centre: ln area_u = ln area_c + delta, with delta from an Earth-fitted conditional model delta = d0 + d1 (lnH_u - lnH_c) + d2 distance + scatter, fitted on Roman towns within 75 km of a centre. Towns farther than 75 km from any centre keep the M1C draw.
model_H.ceiling: No hard cap: the fitted delta distribution decides how often a subordinate town exceeds its centre (6% on Earth near capitals).

validation_declared: Province-blocked folds on the Roman cohort with capitals as centres: held-out (1) share of subordinate towns larger than their centre within 75 km, (2) median size ratio to the centre, (3) whole-cohort KS and total-area ratio as the size gate (KS <= 0.10, ratio 0.80-1.25). Pass if (3) passes and (1), (2) are within 0.05 and a factor 1.25 of the observed. A generator that passes is applied on the map with marked places as centres (owner rule: lore order among marked places stays binding).
caveat: On the map, centres include imperial forts, monasteries and fortified towns, a wider set than Roman provincial capitals; a fortified town is a weaker centre. The fit can include centre class only where Earth evidence exists (capitals); other marked classes are treated as centres by owner rule.

amendments.made_after: scoring the declared delta form (kept as results_delta_form.json): KS 0.096 and area ratio 1.04 pass, but share of subordinates larger than their centre 12.6% vs observed 6.3% and median ratio 0.082 vs 0.11 fail; M1C alone gives 21.5% and 0.37
amendments.known: The delta form models y_u - y_c; its scatter (sd 1.75) mixes the subordinate's and the centre's residuals, so generating it on top of an already drawn centre double-counts the centre's randomness.
amendments.change: Conditional form: ln area_u = g0 + g1 ln area_c + g2 lnH_u + g3 distance/100 + scatter, fitted on subordinates (centre size observed as a predictor), generated given the generated centre. Same folds, seeds, metrics and pass rule. Development data; post-hoc reformulation disclosed.
